text:
alex.cole: :rotating_light: Seeing a spike of node flaps in us-west-2, multiple containers restarting with 'CUDA illegal memory access' errors. Customers reporting request errors and elevated 5xx. Root cause looks like a misaligned pagewalk during recent kernel driver churn.

incident-bot: ALERT: GPU Node Crash Alert (us-west-2). 14 nodes flapped in last 12m. Symptom: process OOMs + CUDA illegal memory access. Pageresponse required.

sophia.lee: Thanks, digging in. I can reproduce on a repro node in staging — attaching a short log.

sophia.lee (code): ```
[2026-03-14T18:02:31Z] runtime: cuda: illegal memory access @ deviceaddr_walk+0x4f
[2026-03-14T18:02:31Z] containerd: task exited: signal: 6
[2026-03-14T18:02:32Z] kernel: vm_fault: bad pte in pagewalk 0x7f9a1c000000
```

maria.gupta: Copying notes from oncall: we saw similar misaligned-offset faults two months ago but those were tied to pinned-buffer eviction + high batch sizes. Current traffic profile shows many long-context requests ( > 4096 tokens ) which can exacerbate KV cache pressure.

ops-shift: We're seeing OOM kills in the serving runtime before the illegal access sometimes. Configs: batch_size=64, max_seq=8192 on these routes. I'm going to scale the pool down to batch=16 for affected model routes.

alex.cole: Good. Quick mitigation plan: 1) Reduce batching for model variant 'redwood-tiny-long' on us-west-2 -> immediate. 2) Enable CPU-fallback shard for canary traffic (route-level). 3) Cordon/drain the worst nodes and repro the kernel trace. 4) Notify customers with potential impact.

sophia.lee: Executing step 1 now. kubectl patch configmap serving-config -n prod --type=merge -p '{"data":{"batch_size":"16"}}'

sophia.lee (code): ```
# one-liners
kubectl get nodes -l gpu=redwood -o wide
kubectl cordon ip-10-0-45-23
kubectl drain ip-10-0-45-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```

oncall: @oncall taking handoff for live mitigation. I will coordinate node cordon/drain and customer comms.

oncall: Sent initial status to stakeholders: "We've seen intermittent GPU kernel pagewalk faults causing container crashes. Immediate mitigations in progress (batching reduced, limited CPU-fallback enabled). Working on node-level repro and kernel trace. More updates in 30m." :mailbox_with_mail:

maria.gupta: For triage - please capture dmesg + GPU driver logs before reboot. If you can reproduce, set env CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 for the runtime to get better stack. Also preserve core dumps (we'll need nvcore).

gpu-team: Noted. We're scheduling a canary kernel module rollback on 2 nodes after cordon. If rollback avoids the illegal access, we'll roll back the kernel driver across the pool.

alex.cole: Customer impact assessment: ~0.8% of production qps in us-west-2 affected (3 customers with elevated errors, one big client at 4% error rate). Severity: P2->P1 if errors persist. Ops, please prepare a short status page entry.

ops-shift: Status page draft: "Investigating GPU node instability in us-west-2 causing intermittent errors for subset of customers. Mitigations: reduced batching and fallback enabled. No data loss. Next update in 30 minutes." Want to send?

oncall: Send the status page. Also ping product for customer outreach on the largest affected tenant. @maria.gupta can you take that?

maria.gupta: On it. Reached out to account team and started a private incident note for the customer.

sophia.lee: Update: after reducing batch size and enabling fallback, we see error rate drop by ~70% on canary traffic. Still repro on one node during heavy long-context requests. Collecting perf counters.

sophia.lee (code): ```
# perf counters snapshot
nvmlDeviceGetVNodeErrorCounter: 0x12
pagewalk_misaligned_count: 47
kernel_addr_walk_fail: 3
```

incident-bot: NOTE: Reminder to capture logs + core dumps before rebooting nodes. Use /incident save-archive <thread_ts>.

oncall: We're going to cordon three nodes (most recent flaps) and repro on an isolated machine with debug kernel. If repro succeeds, we'll roll back driver. If not, we'll escalate to HW/driver vendor.

alex.cole: One more action: enable route-level fallback to 'redwood-tiny-short' (lower mem) for 10% traffic across us-west-2 until we patch. That should reduce load on KV cache and avoid pathological pagewalks.

gpu-team: We're prepping a hotpatch for the kernel pager in a staging build but safety review will take ~2-3h. If rollback proves clean, we prefer that for speed.

oncall: Next update in 20m. Posting an interim note in the incident channel and marking this thread for postmortem owners: sophia.lee, gpu-team, ops-shift.

sophia.lee: Thanks all. Will follow up with repro steps and attach traces. :thumbsup:

maria.gupta: Customer comms sent. No escalations yet.

alex.cole: Closing the loop here: mitigation holding, error rate trending down. Will keep cordons in place until we've verified kernel behavior in staging. Postmortem owners as noted.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Mitigations applied (batch-size reduced, CPU-fallback enabled, targeted node cordons). Error rate reduced by 70% on canary. Ongoing: kernel module rollback verification.
